content.value_statement: Large or vague projects are difficult to start and coordinate. This skill turns clear requirements into ordered tasks with dependencies, acceptance criteria, and checkpoints.
actual_capabilities: Reviews requirements and relevant codebase patterns before planning.
Maps dependencies and orders foundational work before dependent tasks.
Divides features into small, testable vertical slices.
Defines acceptance criteria, verification steps, likely files, dependencies, and scope for each task.
Identifies checkpoints, risks, open questions, and parallel work opportunities.
Produces a plan document and checklist for the tasks directory.
limitations: Requires a specification or clear requirements before task breakdown begins.
Produces planning documents and does not implement the planned code.
Uses file-count scope estimates rather than guaranteed time or cost estimates.
Suggested files and verification commands require validation against the actual project.

use_cases.title: Plan a Feature
use_cases.description: Turn a product specification into ordered implementation tasks with clear acceptance criteria.

use_cases.title: Estimate Project Scope
use_cases.description: Expose dependencies, risks, likely files, and task sizes before committing engineering resources.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Parallel Work
use_cases.description: Separate independent work from sequential dependencies and add shared review checkpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Break Down a Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Break this feature request into ordered tasks. Add acceptance criteria, verification steps, dependencies, likely files, and scope for each task: [requirements]
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a clear feature request that feels too large to start.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Codebase-Aware Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [specification] and the relevant codebase. Create a plan and checklist with dependency-ordered vertical slices and checkpoints.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when repository patterns and existing architecture should guide the plan.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Parallel Delivery
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan [project]. Surface architecture decisions, risks, open questions, sequential dependencies, and safe parallel work for [team or agents].
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when several engineers or agents will implement the work.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Under Constraints
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an implementation plan for [specification] under [constraints]. Prioritize risky assumptions, define contract boundaries, and place reviews before dependent work.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for complex delivery with technical, staffing, or release constraints.

output_examples.input: Add email sign-in to an existing web application.
output: Task 1: Confirm authentication contracts and migration requirements.
Task 2: Add the sign-in service path with focused tests.
Task 3: Add the sign-in interface and end-to-end verification.
Checkpoint: Run tests, build the application, and review the complete sign-in flow.

output_examples.input: Plan searchable orders with filters and pagination.
output: Foundation: Define query parameters, response shape, and database indexes.
Feature slice: Implement search with one filter from storage through the interface.
Expansion: Add remaining filters and pagination after the contract checkpoint.
Risk: Validate query performance with representative order volume.

output_examples.input: Split a reporting project across three agents.
output: Sequential work: Define the shared report contract and data model first.
Parallel work: Assign independent export, interface, and documentation tasks after contract approval.
Coordination: Review integration after each parallel task reaches its acceptance criteria.

best_practices: Provide clear requirements and relevant codebase context before requesting a plan.
Keep tasks small enough to implement, test, and verify in one focused session.
Review architecture decisions, risks, and open questions before implementation starts.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a broad feature name as a complete task.
Do not parallelize tasks that depend on an undefined shared contract.
Do not begin implementation before acceptance criteria and verification steps are approved.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when clear requirements need decomposition, dependency ordering, scope estimates, or coordination across several sessions.

faq.question: Does this skill write implementation code?
faq.answer: No. It creates planning documents and task checklists before implementation begins.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the specification, constraints, relevant repository context, expected behavior, and known risks.

faq.question: How are tasks sized?
faq.answer: Tasks are estimated by scope and likely file count. Large tasks should be divided into smaller vertical slices.

faq.question: Can tasks run in parallel?
faq.answer: Yes. Independent feature slices can run in parallel after shared contracts and sequential dependencies are resolved.

faq.question: What files does the skill produce?
faq.answer: It uses tasks/plan.md for the implementation plan and tasks/todo.md for the checklist.
